_about: Who a search query is from, for the Task 7 split of the Search Console Performance export.
Source: the RAS Landlord SEO Task Brief (rev 9): its keyword table, its 'Terms we do not want to rank for' list and its 'Who we want / Who we do not want' paragraph.

Edit the lists, not classify.js. A phrase matches whole words, case-insensitive, after the query is lower-cased and its hyphens and punctuation turned into spaces ('lead-safe' reads as 'lead safe'). Apostrophes are kept, so 'tenant' does not match inside "tenant's".
The last word of a phrase may also end in s, 's or s' ('landlord' matches 'landlords' and "landlord's"). List any other variant separately.
A phrase written as {"phrase": ..., "unless": [...]} does not count when the query also contains one of the 'unless' phrases.

How a query is classed: landlord phrases only -> landlord; tenant phrases only -> tenant; both -> ambiguous (a conflict, both rules recorded); neither -> ambiguous (any generic phrase recorded). A match that lies wholly inside a longer match is dropped first, so 'my landlord' (tenant) wins over the 'landlord' inside it, and "tenant's rights" (tenant) over "tenant's".
Generic phrases never decide a class on their own. They are recorded so the reviewer can see why a query was left ambiguous.
Flags do not change the class. They mark the other people the brief says we do not want (job seekers, lawyers, 'free', 'apply myself').

keywordTable._source: Brief, 'Keyword targets, one owner page per cluster': every primary and supporting term, verbatim.
phrases: what to do when tenant doesn't pay rent philadelphia
how to get a rental license in philadelphia

signals._source: Landlord-side wording: the owner speaking about their tenant or their property's compliance.

negativeList._source: Brief, 'Terms we do not want to rank for, ever' (the organic negative list), verbatim, plus the word-order and apostrophe variants a searcher types for the same thing.

firstPerson._source: First-person renter wording: the searcher is the one who owes the rent.

generic._source: Words both sides search. On their own they leave a query ambiguous.

pagesForTenants._source: Pages where a tenant click is the point (brief: send tenant queries to /tenants/). Their tenant clicks are reported, not listed as copy-change candidates. Paths, matched against the page URL's path.

flags._source: Brief, 'Who we do not want': a job seeker, a lawyer, anyone searching 'free' or 'apply myself'. Recorded in the flags column; the class is unchanged.
